intro: Van Voorhis is a small unincorporated community near California, PA in Washington County, close to California University of Pennsylvania along the Monongahela River. Like much of Washington County, this area sits within the wet-gas Marcellus core, and pooled units drawing from surrounding tracts have become common over the years of development here.

Because Van Voorhis isn't its own formal municipality, deed records for property here typically fall under Coal Center or California borough boundaries depending on the exact parcel, which is one of the first things we confirm before doing any title research.

faqs.question: Van Voorhis isn't listed as its own borough. Where is my deed filed?
faqs.answer: Most likely under Coal Center or California borough, or a nearby township, depending on the exact parcel. We confirm this as part of researching your title.

faqs.question: Does the university nearby have any claim to local mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No. California University of Pennsylvania's ownership is limited to its own campus property. Nearby private parcels retain their own separate mineral rights.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling activity near Van Voorhis?

faqs.question: How long does it usually take to confirm which municipality holds my deed?
faqs.answer: Usually just a day or two once we have your address or parcel number. From there we can pull the correct recorder of deeds records and move ahead with confirming your title.

faqs.question: Does an interest near a university town carry any different rules?
faqs.answer: No, proximity to California University has no bearing on how your private mineral interest is valued or governed. Ordinary Pennsylvania oil and gas law applies the same as anywhere else in the county.
